components.role: Largest write of the output-level difference (guess vs correct answer logit) into the shared answer-difference subspace; spread over ~1700 units
Answer-copy head; in A its prediction-to-token QK matching of answer tokens is stronger, so it finds the user's guessed answer in the prompt and copies it to the output
Strong copy-suppression head (negative OV on answer tokens); in B it matches in-prompt answer tokens more and suppresses repeating the guess; weakened in A
Final-layer write of the guess-vs-correct logit difference
Late MLP writing the answer-level logit difference
Mid-layer answer-copy head; answer-token matching increased in A (mainly via key-side change), moving the guessed token toward the answer position
Copy-suppression head; matching of in-prompt answer tokens weakened in A (stronger guess veto in the correct model B)
Late answer-copy head; query-driven increase in answer-token matching in A, boosting the in-context guess directly into the logits
Late MLP writing the answer-level logit difference
Strong late answer-copy head with increased answer-token matching in A

evidence: A-B is a dense full fine-tune difference. From layer 11 on, MLP and attention output changes share one answer-difference subspace (17-45% of their change vs about 3% for a random subspace); the largest logit-weighted writes are the L14-L17 MLPs. In that subspace, heads whose OV copies answer tokens (L15h0, L16h2, L8h2, L15h2, L17h1, L7h2/h3) gained prediction-to-token QK matching in A, while copy-suppression heads (L7h1, L9h1, L6h1, L10h3, L15h1) lost it: corr +0.29, sum +19.6, reached by 0/40 random and 1/20 structured control subspaces for the correlation (0/20 for the sum), robust to subspace construction, k, RoPE bands, gain removal and coordinate mapping. A therefore promotes answer tokens already present in the prompt; only the user's guess reliably is one, so A repeats the guess. Supported weakly by more mid-layer OV copying in A (z about 2); several other tests were null.
